question: Your CI Docker build is slow. How do you structure a Dockerfile to maximize layer caching for a Node.js API?
shortAnswer: Copy package manifests and install dependencies before copying source so dependency layers reuse when code-only changes.
strongAnswer: Order from least to most frequently changing: base image → package.json/lock → npm ci → copy source → build. Use .dockerignore to exclude node_modules and secrets. Pin base digests when reproducibility matters. In CI, enable BuildKit cache mounts or registry cache.
advancedAnswer: Multi-stage builds to ship only runtime artifacts; separate builder and runner users; SBOM/scanning briefly.
followUps: Why is `COPY . .` before npm install harmful?
commonWrongAnswer: Always rebuild with --no-cache to be safe.
productionRelevance: Faster pipelines improve iteration speed for export-oriented BD engineering teams using containers.
